title: Latent Feedback, Distillation Optimizers, and Inference Audits
subtitle: Repeated training · Muon distillation · Adaptive inference · Recurrent networks
intro: At fixed parameter count and training FLOPs, when does latent feedback beat more passes over the data? What happens to Muon in short-run distillation? A third study bounds risk after searching inference budgets. The classic revisits gradient explosion and clipping in RNNs.
window: November 14–17, 2026 (Philadelphia time, including the November 17 arXiv announcements)

articles.paper: Latent Feedback Is a Compute and Data Amplifier
articles.authors: Benhao Huang · Chaitanya Dwivedi · Xuezhe Ma · Alexander Moreno · Hector Liu
articles.title: Spend extra compute on latent feedback or more epochs?
articles.dateNote: v1 submitted November 15, 2026 ET · November 17 announcement
articles.evidence: Read Sections 2–5, Table 1 and Appendix F

blocks.text: Feed the previous token’s top-layer state back into the current input. Training approximates this recurrence with one or two parallel passes and computes loss and gradients only on the last pass. The comparison holds fixed non-embedding parameters N, unique tokens U and FLOP budget F, measured in vanilla Transformer epochs over U. [1]

blocks.label: Feedback uses cₛ times the baseline’s training FLOPs per token, leaving Rₛ epochs under the same budget.
Paper’s fitted law. For Rₛ<1, Dₛ=URₛ. The capacity multiplier vₛ is 1 for the vanilla Transformer.

blocks.text: To first order, the capacity multiplier lowers the capacity term, while extra forward passes reduce repeat exposure and raise the data term. The Dolma 3 comparison below matches model size and validation loss, using a budget of two vanilla Transformer epochs and varying unique tokens per non-embedding parameter. [1]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Fitting on 60M–271M models yielded at most 0.29% relative validation-loss error at the held-out 778M size. The comparison constrains deployed model size. If parameter count can grow, a larger equal-compute Transformer has 0.006–0.012 lower loss throughout the fitted grid. [1]

articles.paper: Do Pretraining Optimizer Gains Transfer to KL Distillation?
articles.title: All-2D Muon shows no consistent advantage in short-run KL distillation
articles.dateNote: v1 submitted November 14, 2026 ET · November 17 announcement

blocks.text: Four instruction-tuned Qwen pairs share a tokenizer within each pair. The token-level forward KL compares the fixed teacher q with student p. Training averages the answer region A and reasoning region C separately within each example, so longer reasoning does not take more weight from the answer. [2]

blocks.label: Training objective with both regions present. Validation pools all supervised tokens with equal weight.

blocks.text: The protocol uses 79,535 Nemotron reasoning traces, global batch 144, 1,683 steps and three seeds. All-2D applies spectral updates to embeddings and the output head as well. The table shows comparisons explicitly reported in the paper. [2]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: All completed matrix recipes took more trainer time, which includes teacher inference, validation and checkpointing. The result is for the fixed budget, All-2D parameter assignment and offline traces. Hidden-layer-only Muon and downstream accuracy were outside the comparison. [2]

articles.paper: Anytime-Valid PAC-Bayes Certificates for Adaptive Test-Time Scaling
articles.title: How to bound risk after selecting the sampling budget on calibration data?
articles.dateNote: v1 submitted November 16, 2026 ET · November 17 announcement

blocks.text: A recipe is a randomized predictor combining prompts, sampling budgets, allocation rules and verifiers. The prior P is independent of calibration data. Q may be chosen using the i.i.d. calibration problems and execution records. For losses between 0 and 1, summing fixed-time failures δ/[n(n+1)] gives one event covering every n and Q. [3]

blocks.label: Theorem 4.1. Selecting one of M recipes under a uniform prior costs log M / n. Invert binary kl for the risk upper bound.

Simpler bound from Proposition 6.1 for b independent samples and answer support at most m. If a wrong answer is more probable, the probability of voting correctly instead has an exponentially decaying upper bound.

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: On GSM8K, gpt-4.1-mini selected b=5 from four budgets. With 659 calibration problems, the upper bound was 0.109 and the risk on 660 held-out problems was 0.039. The uniform bound can be loose. The prior and family of recipes must be fixed before inspecting calibration records. [3]

articles.paper: Instructor-designed AI improves learning in a randomized trial across 19 universities
articles.authors: Jun Li · Robert Bray · Sébastien Martin · Hamsa Bastani (Wharton) · et al.
articles.title: Randomized trial of instructor-designed AI
articles.dateNote: v1 submitted November 13, 2026 ET · November 17 announcement

blocks.text: Across 19 universities and about 7,200 students, course-level randomization and a difference-in-differences regression using historical outcomes gave a student-level exam effect of +0.32 SD (95% CI [0.06, 0.59]). Activity and satisfaction showed no significant change. The treatment let instructors design and deploy tools and encompassed heterogeneous interventions. [4]

classic.paper: On the difficulty of training recurrent neural networks
classic.authors: Razvan Pascanu · Tomas Mikolov · Yoshua Bengio
classic.title: Why RNN gradients explode and what clipping controls
classic.dateNote: First arXiv posting November 21, 2012 · Read the ICML 2013 proceedings version

recognition.label: Highly cited in OpenAlex · Checked November 17, 2026

classic.question: At a fixed update cap, if clipping fires often, how could directional Jacobian gains distinguish occasional steep walls from systematic long-range contraction?

blocks.text: Bengio et al. (1994) tied the difficulty of learning long dependencies to gradients that decay across steps. This paper follows Jacobian products in BPTT and distinguishes backward contraction from oversized parameter updates near steep walls in the loss. [23]

blocks.label: The paper’s vanilla RNN parameterization, with input uₜ and hidden state xₜ.

blocks.tex: \frac{\partial E_t}{\partial x_k}=\frac{\partial E_t}{\partial x_t}J_t\cdots J_{k+1},\qquad \|J_t\cdots J_{k+1}\|_2\le (\|W\|_2\Gamma)^{t-k}
blocks.label: Row-gradient convention. If |σ′|≤Γ and the multiplier is below 1, the long-range error signal decays exponentially.
Algorithm 1. The gradient direction is preserved and the Euclidean update is capped at ητ. A zero gradient remains zero.

Soft constraint from Equation (9), encouraging norm preservation along the current nonzero backward direction. The implementation takes the immediate partial derivative, holding states and error signals fixed.

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: Clipping gives an update-norm cap. The norm-preserving penalty targets current error directions, and a long Jacobian product can still contract. [23]
